issues.title: [Feat] [NPU] qwen-image: Adapt Qwen-Image 2.1 on Ascend
issues.body: Part of #43519 (roadmap item: *Qwen-Image-2.1 — adapt the existing SGLang Diffusion pipeline for Ascend*). ## Motivation Qwen-Image 2.1 already runs on Ascend through `torch_npu`, but two hot paths in the DiT stay on the slow eager implementations: `QwenImage21Attention` forces the native fp32 QK RMSNorm on every platform, and the complex RoPE goes through the complex64 multiply path. This PR routes both to the CANN operators exposed by `torch_npu`: - `torch_npu.npu_rms_norm` for `norm_q` / `norm_k`. - `torch_npu.npu_rotary_mul(..., rotary_mode="interleave")` for the complex RoPE, with the cos/sin tables prepared once per layout and cached. Cos/sin for `npu_rotary_mul` must be expanded with `repeat_interleave(2)`; a plain `cat((c, c), -1)` pairs the wrong frequencies. The previously attempted Triton fast-path enablement on NPU is **not** part of this change: the QK-norm+RoPE Triton kernel is not bit-exact for sequence lengths ≥ 1024 and is 60–95× slower than the eager chain on Ascend. The three kernel files touched by that attempt are restored to their pre-enablement state. The result is full Qwen-Image 2.1 coverage on one A3 chip: text-to-image, single- and multi-reference editing, transparent RGBA output, and local recolor, with NPU CI cases and baselines. ## Modifications - `python/sglang/multimodal_gen/runtime/models/dits/qwen_image21.py` - `QwenImage21Attention`: `force_native=not current_platform.is_npu()` for `norm_q` / `norm_k`, so NPU dispatches to `npu_rms_norm` (bit-identical to the native fp32 path in our measurements). - `apply_rope`: NPU branch using `npu_rotary_mul` with cached cos/sin. - `python/sglang/kernels/ops/diffusion/activation/silu_mul_bitexact.py`, `python/sglang/kernels/ops/diffusion/rope/complex_rope_triton.py`, `python/sglang/kernels/ops/diffusion/rope/qknorm_complex_rope_triton.py` - Revert the previous Triton enablement on NPU: restore the CUDA-only guards, drop the `contextlib.nullcontext()` device branch, and remove the added `contextlib` imports. The files are byte-identical to the state before `7e2e7145fa`. - `python/sglang/multimodal_gen/test/server/ascend/testcase_configs_npu.py` - Five `qwen_image21_*` NPU cases with the same sampling contract (1024×1024, png, 40 steps, guidance 1, seed 42, `quality="lossless"`): t2i, single-reference edit, two-reference edit, transparent output, and local recolor. - All five set `run_consistency_check=False` in this commit; the t2i case is switched on together with the NPU GT pin in a follow-up commit once the GT-gen workflow has published its image. - `python/sglang/multimodal_gen/test/server/ascend/perf_baselines_npu.json` - Baselines for the five new cases. - `scripts/ci/utils/diffusion/prefetch_input_image.py` - Also cache the second multi-image reference and export `SGLANG_TEST_MULTI_IMAGE_INPUT_IMAGE`. - `.github/workflows/diffusion-ci-gt-gen-npu.yml` - Run the input prefetch before `gen_diffusion_ci_outputs`, so the reference edit cases can produce their published images. - `python/sglang/srt/environ.py` - `SGLANG_TEST_MULTI_IMAGE_INPUT_IMAGE`. - `docs/cookbook/diffusion/Qwen-Image/Qwen-Image-2.1.mdx` - Add Ascend to the hardware picker note and the recommended-hardware table (no separate platform section, matching the Qwen-Image cookbook layout). - `docs/src/snippets/configs/Qwen/qwen-image-2.1.jsx` - Add Ascend A3 to the deployment picker: Torch SDPA only, resident placement, `--warmup-mode request`. ## Verification CI cases - All five `qwen_image21_*` cases run end-to-end with `run_consistency_check=False` in this commit, so the PR CI does not depend on a GT that does not exist yet. The recolor case edits the shared TI2I image (orange skirt and bow to deep blue). - Follow-up (same PR, after the GT exists): the `diffusion-ci-gt-gen-npu` workflow runs `qwen_image21_t2i_1npu` on the NPU runner and publishes `qwen_image21_t2i_1npu_1gpu.png` to `diffusion-ci/consistency_gt/sglang_generated/ascend/` in `sgl-project/ci-data-diffusion`. A follow-up commit then enables the t2i consistency check and bumps the NPU `test_utils.py` pin to the returned SHA, in the same commit. **No image is uploaded by hand.** - Both edit inputs are staged by `prefetch_input_image.py` (the shared TI2I image and the second multi-image reference) in `pr-test-npu.yml` and in the GT-generation workflow. `direct_url_test=True` is not used on NPU: it asks the model server to fetch the URLs, while the runner-side prefetch keeps the server offline-capable. - NPU perf baselines for all five cases are in `test/server/ascend/perf_baselines_npu.json`, produced on one A3 chip with `python -m sglang.multimodal_gen.test.scripts.gen_perf_baselines --case ...` (not hand-written); the existing 13 entries are untouched. ### Reproduction ```bash # t2i sglang generate --model-path /path/to/Qwen-Image-2.1 \ --prompt "Doraemon is eating dorayaki" \ --num-inference-steps 40 --guidance-scale 1 \ --height 1024 --width 1024 --seed 42 --num-gpus 1 \ --generator-device cuda --save-output ``` ```bash # ti2i (2D -> 3D) sglang generate --model-path /path/to/Qwen-Image-2.1 \ --image-path TI2I_Qwen_Image_Edit_Input.jpg \ --prompt "Convert 2D style to 3D style" \ --num-inference-steps 40 --guidance-scale 1 \ --height 1536 --width 1024 --seed 42 --num-gpus 1 \ --generator-device cuda --save-output ``` ```bash # multi-image edit (two references; edit2509_1.jpg / edit2509_2.jpg from the # Qwen-Image-Edit-2509 test set) curl -sS -X POST http://127.0.0.1:30000/v1/images/edits \ -F "model=/path/to/Qwen-Image-2.1" \ -F "image=@edit2509_1.jpg" -F "image=@edit2509_2.jpg" \ -F "prompt=The magician bear is on the left, the alchemist bear is on the right, facing each other in the central park square." \ -F "size=1024x1024" -F "num_inference_steps=40" -F "guidance_scale=1" \ -F "seed=42" -F "quality=lossless" -F "response_format=b64_json" ``` ```bash # local recolor (CI case): orange skirt and bow -> deep blue curl -sS -X POST http://127.0.0.1:30000/v1/images/edits \ -F "model=/path/to/Qwen-Image-2.1" \ -F "image=@TI2I_Qwen_Image_Edit_Input.jpg" \ -F "prompt=Change the orange skirt and bow to deep blue, keeping her pose, face, hair, and the SGL logo unchanged." \ -F "size=1024x1024" -F "num_inference_steps=40" -F "guidance_scale=1" \ -F "seed=42" -F "quality=lossless" -F "response_format=b64_json" ``` Transparency is an HTTP generation request with `"background": "transparent"`. The CI recolor case uses `/v1/images/edits` with the shared TI2I image; the transparent-cat recolor below is a separate manual check. ## Accuracy Tests Platform: Ascend A3, CANN 9.1.0, torch 2.10.0+cpu / torch_npu 2.10.0.post6. Same chip, same seed, `--generator-device cuda` (device RNG, matching the HTTP CI path). Metrics are the repository's consistency metrics (RGB, alpha ignored). ### t2i: A+B (`npu_rms_norm` + `npu_rotary_mul`) vs eager, seeds 42–47 | seed | SSIM | PSNR (dB) | CLIP | mean_abs_diff | max_abs | MSE | | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | | 42 | 0.9839 | 30.28 | 0.9983 | 1.716 | 236 | 60.91 | | 43 | 0.9885 | 36.65 | 0.9963 | 1.571 | 139 | 14.05 | | 44 | 0.9881 | 37.43 | 0.9968 | 1.216 | 95 | 11.76 | | 45 | 0.9777 | 30.58 | 0.9947 | 2.225 | 248 | 56.91 | | 46 | 0.9695 | 28.91 | 0.9903 | 3.140 | 223 | 83.55 | | 47 | 0.9711 | 27.18 | 0.9901 | 3.169 | 219 | 124.34 | Repository thresholds: CLIP ≥ 0.92, SSIM ≥ 0.95, PSNR ≥ 28 dB, mean_abs_diff ≤ 8. All six seeds pass CLIP and mean_abs_diff; five of six pass SSIM; seed 47 is 0.82 dB below the PSNR threshold (mean_abs_diff 3.17, well inside). Visual inspection: the subject, shape and colors are preserved; differences are pixel-level. ### ti2i: 2D → 3D style conversion (A+B) Input is the shared CI edit image `TI2I_Qwen_Image_Edit_Input.jpg` (sha256 `0d56a63fca6ef8fe2a0ca27a0774c2bada9b2a198aeedbfdfb23bec09d0d3901`), prompt `Convert 2D style to 3D style`, seed 42, 40 steps, guidance 1. End-to-end on one A3 chip (A+B, `quality="lossless"`): 23.1 s at 1024×1024 (denoise 16.69 s, 0.417 s/step, decode 2.79 s) and 36.8 s at 1536×1024 (denoise 28.25 s, 0.706 s/step, decode 4.74 s). ### multi-image editing (A+B) Two reference images (`edit2509_1.jpg` magician bear, `edit2509_2.jpg` alchemist bear, from the Qwen-Image-Edit-2509 test set), sent as two `image` fields to HTTP `/v1/images/edits`; seed 42, 40 steps, guidance 1, 1024×1024, `quality="lossless"`. The server log confirms the request carries both paths. - **Composition** — with the multi-image CI prompt ("The magician bear is on the left, the alchemist bear is on the right, facing each other in the central park square."), both identities are preserved (hat/robe/book/wand, graduation cap/cauldron/fan/Qwen shirt) and placed as instructed. - **Slot binding** — with "the bear from image 1 … image 2 …", uploading `[ref1, ref2]` puts ref1 on the left and ref2 on the right; uploading `[ref2, ref1]` swaps them. The second file lands in ``; it is not silently dropped or merged into the first. - **Ablation** — one reference at a time produces only that subject. - **Determinism** — repeating the request, or running it on a different chip, reproduces a byte-identical PNG. The CI case uses the two references staged for the NPU runner (the shared TI2I image and `rabbit.jpg`); the bear pair above is the manual slot-binding check. | request | CLIP | SSIM | PSNR (dB) | mean_abs | | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | | official (2 refs, CI prompt) | 0.9793 | 0.8285 | 17.78 | 10.182 | | order [1,2] | 0.9983 | 0.9631 | 26.58 | 1.972 | | order [2,1] | 0.9913 | 0.8986 | 21.39 | 5.811 | | ref 1 only | 0.9995 | 0.9947 | 39.80 | 0.666 | | ref 2 only | 0.9986 | 0.9768 | 25.97 | 1.992 | Differences vs eager concentrate on anti-aliased outlines and glyphs, with no structural or identity change (the amplified diff maps are edge-only). issues.title: [Feat] [AMD] diffusion: Enable residual_gate_add fast path on ROCm
issues.body:
<!-- Thank you for your contribution! Please follow these guidelines to enhance your pull request. If anything is unclear, submit your PR and reach out to maintainers for assistance. Join our Slack community at https://slack.sglang.io to discuss further. -->

## Motivation

On ROCm, the existing `residual_gate_add` Triton kernels embed NVIDIA PTX (`cvt.rn.bf16.f32` / `cvt.rn.f16.f32`, constraint `"=h"`). AMDGPU does not support the `h` register class, so LLVM aborts during compilation instead of raising a Python exception. The diffusion worker can therefore terminate during denoising before the eager fallback is reached.

<!-- Describe the purpose and goals of this pull request. -->

## Modifications

This PR adds a dedicated ROCm Triton fast path while preserving the existing CUDA implementation.

- CUDA keeps the existing JIT/custom-op path and NVIDIA PTX rounding helper, now named `_cuda_round16_f32`.
- ROCm uses a separate custom op and Triton kernels for flat and transposed layouts.
- The ROCm flat kernel also handles batched `[B, 1, D]` gates, including LTX-2's strided AdaLN views.
- ROCm BF16 rounding uses `round_bf16_to_fp32`.
- ROCm FP16 rounding uses opaque `v_cvt_f16_f32` inline assembly because a normal FP32 → FP16 → FP32 cast can be folded away by Triton.
- CUDA and ROCm use separate predicates and rounding helpers. Unsupported inputs continue to use the eager fallback.
- Existing residual-gate tests now dispatch to the appropriate backend, with a regression test ensuring HIP never enters the CUDA/PTX path.

<!-- Detail the changes made in this pull request. -->

## Accuracy Tests

On gfx1151, the ROCm path was compared against the eager reference with exact comparison for FP16 and BF16.

Coverage includes FP16/BF16/FP32, full/row-broadcast/per-token/batched gates, transposed layouts, storage offsets, graph/compile paths, and unsupported-input fallback.



## Speed Tests

gfx1151 (Radeon 8060S), ROCm 7.2.4, PyTorch 2.9.1, Triton 3.7.0.
Row-broadcast gate, wall-clock time per call:

| dtype | shape | eager | ROCm path | speedup |
|---|---|---:|---:|---:|
| bf16 | `[1, 4096, 3072]` | 560.6 µs | 333.6 µs | 1.68x |
| bf16 | `[1, 4202, 3072]` | 568.8 µs | 341.6 µs | 1.67x |
| fp16 | `[1, 4096, 3072]` | 563.5 µs | 330.5 µs | 1.71x |
| fp16 | `[1, 4202, 3072]` | 572.3 µs | 339.4 µs | 1.69x |

These measurements cover the row-broadcast path only; the transposed ROCm path has not been independently profiled on AMD, so no speedup is claimed for that layout.

<!-- If this pull request impacts inference speed, provide benchmarking and profiling results. -->

## Test Results

| Validation | Before | After |
|---|---|---|
| `residual_gate_add` standalone | ROCm process aborts while compiling NVIDIA PTX | ROCm Triton path matches eager |
| Residual-gate test cases | Process terminated at the first case | All 55 ROCm residual-gate cases pass |
| Unsupported ROCm inputs | Eager fallback only | Unsupported inputs still use the eager fallback |

Only gfx1151 was validated locally. gfx942 and gfx950 remain for AMD CI.
CUDA was not run locally; its implementation was preserved unchanged.

issues.title: [Fix] [AMD] diffusion: materialize SDPA operands for long sequences
issues.body:
## Motivation

`SDPAImpl.forward` transposes the `[B, S, H, D]` activations into the `[B, H, S, D]` layout `scaled_dot_product_attention` expects. That transpose is always a strided view, and AOTriton's flash path only applies to **dense** operands, so on HIP a long-sequence attention silently falls back to a generic kernel.

Measured on gfx1151 (AMD Ryzen AI MAX+ 395, 32 heads x 128, bf16, one SDPA call):

| S | strided | dense | gain |
|---|---|---|---|
| 1024 | 1.39 ms | 1.18 ms | 1.18x |
| 2048 | 4.75 ms | 4.35 ms | 1.09x |
| 4096 | 20.84 ms | 15.99 ms | 1.30x |
| 8192 | 184.2 ms | 61.2 ms | 3.01x |
| 16384 | 2255 ms | 242.9 ms | **9.28x** |

The cliff is at S=8192: below it the strided layout still reaches the flash kernel (13-15 TFLOPS), above it drops to 2 TFLOPS while the dense operands hold 18 TFLOPS.

## Modifications

- Extract `sdpa_operands()` from `SDPAImpl.forward`. It still returns the heads-first view, and on HIP it materializes the operands **when `S >= 8192`**.
- The copy is layout-only: values are bit-identical, so there is no accuracy change.
- Below the threshold nothing changes. Qwen-Image 2.1 at 1024^2 (S=4096) is 5.7% *slower* when the copy is unconditional, because the per-layer allocation costs more than the 1.3x kernel gain - so the gate is a sequence threshold, not just a device check.
- The common path (CUDA, and short sequences on any device) keeps the zero-copy view and is the first branch.

## Accuracy Tests

- `python/sglang/multimodal_gen/test/unit/test_sdpa_operand_layout.py` (new, runs in the `diffusion-unit-1-gpu-h100` suite): heads-first layout and values; short sequences keep the zero-copy view; long sequences are dense only on HIP; the copy preserves every bit (`torch.equal` against the transposed view).
- End to end, the change only moves tensor layout, so no numerical change is expected by construction. Verified on Qwen-Image 2.1 at 1024^2 and 2048^2 with a fixed seed: identical image, no metric shift.

## Speed Tests and Profiling

Qwen-Image 2.1, default environment, `torch_sdpa` backend, gfx1151. Seconds per denoising step (mean over all steps), two runs per arm:

| Shape | before | after | gain |
|---|---|---|---|
| 1024^2 / 20 steps | 3.8524 | 3.8523 | 1.00x |
| 2048^2 / 12 steps | 78.04 / 77.42 | 22.04 / 22.11 | **3.54x** |

Within-arm spread <1%. The 2048^2 gain is AOTriton flash instead of the generic kernel; the 1024^2 row confirms the threshold leaves short sequences untouched.

## Checklist

- [x] Format your code according to the Format code with pre-commit (`isort` + `ruff` pass).
- [x] Add unit tests according to the Run and add unit tests.
- [ ] Update documentation according to Write documentations (no user-facing docs describe this backend detail).
- [x] Provide accuracy and speed benchmark results.
- [x] Follow the SGLang code style guidance.

issues.title: [Diffusion] Add Cache-DiT support for SenseNova-U1
issues.body: Part of #37742 ## Motivation SenseNova-U1 currently cannot use Cache-DiT acceleration in SGLang. Unlike conventional diffusion transformers, SenseNova-U1 shares its Qwen3 decoder between prefix processing, Think/text generation, KV-cache updates, and iterative image denoising. Applying Cache-DiT to the entire decoder would therefore affect non-denoising paths and could corrupt the prefix or KV-cache state. This PR adds request-scoped Cache-DiT support that routes only pure image denoising forwards through the cached decoder blocks while preserving the native decoder layers for all other paths. Key Value & Quantifiable Benefits: 🚀 **2.76× Speedup**: Reduces the mean end-to-end latency for 2048×2048 image generation from 62.26s to 22.54s, with request throughput increasing proportionally by 2.76×. 🎯 **Negligible Accuracy Loss**: Rigorous evaluation on the LongText-Bench dataset shows an absolute score difference of only 0.3 points (from 99.8 to 99.5, a ~0.33% relative difference). issues.title: [Fix] diffusion: keep TP/Ulysses head shards on the unsharded torch SDPA kernel
issues.body:
## Motivation

PyTorch's flash SDPA forward picks split-KV when `batch * heads * ceil(query_len / 128)` is below 80% of the SM count (`num_splits_heuristic` in ATen's `flash_api.cpp`). Split-KV reorders the softmax sums. Tensor parallelism and Ulysses both reduce the number of heads each rank attends over. At short sequence lengths, that can push a head shard onto the split kernel while the unsharded layer stays unsplit. The result is that `--attention-backend torch_sdpa` runs differ between parallel and single-GPU execution even at the attention-operator level.

The default backends do not depend on the head count, and are unaffected:
- sm100: cuDNN SDPA. Measured on B200: head shards are bit-identical.
- sm90: sgl FA3, which runs with `num_splits=1`.

Affected setups:
- explicit `--attention-backend torch_sdpa`;
- sm120, where torch SDPA is the default;
- head dims that fall back to torch SDPA.

This came up while validating Ovis-Image (#43152), which carries a model-local version of this fix.

## Modifications

- **`SDPAImpl`** pads query rows past the split threshold when all of the following hold:
  - the request asks for `quality="exact"`;
  - the call is a non-causal, unmasked fp16/bf16 CUDA call, without dropout and with head_dim ≤ 256;
  - the local head count would split, but the unsharded layer's would not.

  Query rows attend independently, so the real rows match the unsharded kernel bit for bit. The padding is sliced off afterwards.
- **Gated on `exact`**: under the quality tiers, the default `lossless` tier already allows rounding-order changes. It keeps the faster split kernel and is unchanged by this PR.
- **`USPAttention`** accepts `global_num_heads`, the layer's head count before TP sharding, and forwards it to the impl. It defaults to `num_heads`, which already covers Ulysses-only sharding.
- **TP-sharding DiTs** pass their pre-TP head count: FLUX, FLUX.2, Qwen-Image, Anima, Wan, HunyuanVideo, Z-Image.
- **Unchanged**: `CudnnSDPAImpl` / `DynamicCudnnSDPAImpl`, explicit cuDNN priority, masked/causal calls, FA varlen and ring paths.
- **Tests**:
  - `test/unit/test_sdpa_sharded_heads.py`: head shards vs the unsharded output, plus every case that must not pad.
  - `test/single_test_file/test_usp_sdpa_sharded_heads_2_gpu.py`: real Ulysses2 `USPAttention` vs a single rank.

## Accuracy Tests

**Attention operator** (B200, bf16, head_dim 128, 24 global heads, exact tier). The table shows the fraction of output elements that differ from the unsharded 24-head flash SDPA:

| local heads \ query length | 1025 | 1536 | 2560 | 4608 |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 12, before | 41% | exact | exact | exact |
| 6, before | 41% | 35% | exact | exact |
| 3, before | 41% | 41% | 35% | 42% |
| any, with this PR | exact | exact | exact | exact |

![op sweep](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/fusheng-ji/sglang/699cd5ab302193bec227cf4f22218aa8bb2a812f/op-sweep.png)

**Real Ulysses2 `USPAttention` (2 × B200).** Compared against a single-rank SDPA on the full sequence:

| heads / seq | before | with this PR |
|---|---|---|
| 24 / 1024 | about 619k elements differ (max 2.0e-3) | bit-identical |
| 12 / 1536 | about 411k elements differ (max 9.8e-4) | bit-identical |

**Same-input transformer forward, TP2 vs 1 GPU** (real weights, one step, torch SDPA, 1088-token joint sequence). Other TP effects, such as row-parallel reductions, dominate the remaining difference:

| Model | max abs, before → after | differing elements, before → after |
|---|---|---|
| FLUX.1-dev | 0.031 → 0.031 | 43,617 → 43,375 |
| Qwen-Image | 0.094 → 0.063 | 43,959 → 43,996 |

**End-to-end images** (exact tier, torch SDPA). FLUX.1-dev at 384² / 28 steps and Qwen-Image at 512² / 30 steps, so that 2-way head shards cross the split threshold. Mean absolute pixel difference against 1 GPU, over seeds:

| Model / topology | before (mean ± std) | with this PR (mean ± std) |
|---|---|---|
| FLUX.1-dev TP2 | 4.81 ± 0.60 | 4.26 ± 0.27 |
| FLUX.1-dev Ulysses2 | 3.48 ± 0.88 | 4.44 ± 0.65 |
| Qwen-Image TP2 | 2.10 ± 0.85 | 1.80 ± 0.50 |
| Qwen-Image Ulysses2 | 2.19 ± 1.27 | 1.97 ± 1.02 |

Values are mean absolute pixel difference on a 0–255 scale over 5 seeds (42, 1, 2, 3, 4). The figures show seed 42; the bottom rows are |diff| ×16.

![FLUX.1-dev](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/fusheng-ji/sglang/699cd5ab302193bec227cf4f22218aa8bb2a812f/e2e-flux.jpg)

![Qwen-Image](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/fusheng-ji/sglang/699cd5ab302193bec227cf4f22218aa8bb2a812f/e2e-qwen.jpg)

**This PR does not claim an end-to-end improvement.** Every parallel image is visually equivalent to the single-GPU one, both before and after the change. The pixel differences come from many small rounding differences that the denoising loop amplifies, and they vary strongly between seeds. Over 5 seeds:
- TP2 is slightly closer to 1 GPU.
- Qwen-Image Ulysses2 is unchanged within noise.
- FLUX.1-dev Ulysses2 is slightly further away; 4 of 5 seeds got worse.

Other parallel effects, such as GEMM shapes and reductions, still separate the runs. What this PR guarantees is narrower: under the exact tier, the attention operator no longer changes with the head sharding.

Unit tests: the new unit and 2-GPU tests fail without the change and pass with it; 146 related USP/attention unit tests pass.

## Speed Tests and Profiling

Padding only triggers for exact-tier requests at short sequence lengths with sharded heads. Single attention call, B200:

| local heads / seq | padded to | before | exact tier with this PR |
|---|---|---|---|
| 12 / 1088 | 1280 | 58 µs | 61 µs |
| 6 / 1088 | 2560 | 34 µs | 65 µs |
| 6 / 1536 | 2560 | 39 µs | 118 µs |
| 12 or 6 / 4608 | not padded | unchanged | unchanged |

The `lossless` (default) and `high` tiers are unaffected.

## Not covered

- sm120 and sm90 were not run on hardware. On sm90 the default FA3 path is unaffected by construction (`num_splits=1`); sm120 uses the same PyTorch flash heuristic with its own SM count.
- The component-accuracy harness gives every rank the full token set under SP. Its Ulysses whole-model comparison against 1 GPU is therefore not like-for-like and is not reported. Ulysses is covered by the real 2-GPU test above.

## Checklist

- [x] Format code with pre-commit.
- [x] Add unit tests.
- [x] Update documentation (docstrings).
- [x] Provide accuracy and speed benchmark results.
- [x] Follow the SGLang code style guidance.

### Update (2026-10-14)

- **Rebased onto current `main`** (force-pushed). Conflict in `USPAttention.__init__`: `main` added `capture_dense_attention`; both parameters are kept.
- **Two more head-sharding call sites pass `global_num_heads`:** LLaDA-Image, which landed on `main` after this PR's base, and the MOVA dual-tower bridge cross-attention, which shards heads over TP but lives outside `models/dits/`.

**Service-level check.** FLUX.1-dev HTTP server, `torch_sdpa`, TP 1/2/4/8, 512x512 and 1024x1024, 20 steps, `quality` lossless and exact, PR head vs its parent (`214347891a`). An in-server probe saved sampled SDPA calls on every rank at steps 0 and 10 (108 calls). Offline, each call was rerun with all heads concatenated on one B200 with the flash backend pinned, and every rank's head slice was compared bitwise:

| Calls | parent | this PR |
| --- | --- | --- |
| shard does not cross the split threshold (all TP2, TP4 at 1024²), lossless and exact | 24/24 equal | 24/24 equal |
| shard crosses the threshold (TP4 at 512², all TP8), `exact` | 0/18 equal | 18/18 equal |
| shard crosses the threshold, `lossless` | 0/12 equal | 0/12 equal (split kernel kept by design) |

Lossless images are byte-identical between the parent and this PR at every TP size, and all images are identical at TP1. TP2 never crosses the threshold at these shapes, so it only shows there is no regression. The service check ran on the pre-rebase head `9b4fa9eea2`; the FLUX code path is unchanged by the rebase.

Unit and two-GPU tests on the rebased head (B200): `test_sdpa_sharded_heads.py` and `test_usp_sdpa_sharded_heads_2_gpu.py`, 4 passed, 81 subtests passed.

### Re-verification (2026-10-15)

On the rebased head: `test_sdpa_sharded_heads.py` and `test_usp_sdpa_sharded_heads_2_gpu.py` 4 passed, 81 subtests passed, 0 skipped, on a B200 host with two GPUs (148 SMs, so the test's split cases are not skipped); `pre-commit run --all-files` passes (Rust hooks skipped: no `cargo` here, no Rust files touched). The service-level check above was run on the pre-rebase head `9b4fa9eea2` and has not been repeated on the rebased head. The offline recomputation first used PyTorch's default SDPA backend and matched nothing; it was corrected to pin the flash backend the server runs and re-run on the same saved probe data, with the single call checked by hand against every backend first.

### Update (2026-10-15)

Re-ran against current `main` (`e87e32b311`) on a local merge of this head, which merges without conflicts: `test_sdpa_sharded_heads.py` and `test_usp_sdpa_sharded_heads_2_gpu.py` 4 passed, 81 subtests passed, 0 skipped, on a two-GPU B200 host. The branch itself is unchanged, and the service-level check above is still the one run on the pre-rebase head.

issues.body:
Motivation

Qwen-Image 2.1's FFN activation fast path (fused_silu_mul_bitexact) is gated on current_platform.is_cuda(). On ROCm that predicate is False (PlatformEnum.ROCM), so the optimization is dead code on AMD hardware — even though the fused kernel is plain Triton (no CUDA JIT / PTX) and reproduces the eager silu(a) * b chain bit-exactly on HIP.

This is the same situation the XPU port fixed in #41940, which enabled the identical kernel via (x.is_cuda or x.is_xpu). This PR does the equivalent for ROCm/HIP.

Modifications

python/sglang/multimodal_gen/runtime/models/dits/qwen_image21.py:

  • Add _silu_mul_device = current_platform.is_cuda() or current_platform.is_hip().

  • Gate QwenImage21FeedForward.forward on _silu_mul_device instead of the vendor-pure _is_cuda.

Every other fast path in the module (RoPE, QK-norm, packed QKV, SDPA) stays CUDA-only, because those really are CUDA JIT / PTX kernels. The existing BitExactFusionGate still self-verifies the first call and permanently disables the path on any mismatch, so a platform that turns out not to be bit-exact falls back to eager instead of diverging.

python/sglang/multimodal_gen/test/unit/test_qwen_image21_silu_mul_fusion.py (new):

  • assert the guard tracks the CUDA-like device family;

  • assert fused_silu_mul_bitexact is bit-exact vs F.silu(a) * b at the FFN activation shapes.

Accuracy Tests

Environment: AMD Ryzen AI MAX 395 (Strix Halo), Radeon 8060S Graphics, gfx1151 (RDNA 3.5), torch 2.9.1+rocm7.2.4 (hip 7.2.53211), SGLang Diffusion, attention backend torch_sdpa.

issues.title: [diffusion] cache: add DPCache, calibrated key-timestep caching
issues.body:
## Motivation

This PR adds DPCache, training-free key-timestep caching driven by an offline-calibrated schedule. It adapts [Denoising as Path Planning: Training-Free Acceleration of Diffusion Models with DPCache](https://arxiv.org/abs/2602.22654); the algorithm is credited to that paper.

A request carries a schedule of `K` full steps. Those steps run the whole transformer block stack. On every other step, DPCache extrapolates the final block feature from the two most recent full steps and runs only the output head, using the current timestep. Every scheduler update still runs and the weights are unchanged, so this is approximate inference, not distillation or a reduced-step sampler.

On Qwen-Image 2.1 (1024x1024, 40 steps, one RTX 5090), `K=20` is **1.97x faster end to end** with mean LPIPS 0.0076 against native output. That is 10.9% less time than the conservative Cache-DiT preset, with lower mean and max LPIPS. `K=12` is **3.21x faster**.

DPCache plugs in the same way as Spectrum and TeaCache: a mixin on `CachableDiT`. Any DiT can opt in; Qwen-Image 2.1 is the first. A schedule is calibrated per deployment, so the server owns the schedules and a request only picks a budget. A calibration tool builds the schedules.

```bash
# 1. calibrate once per checkpoint and request configuration
python -m sglang.multimodal_gen.tools.dpcache_calibrate record --model-path MODEL \
  --prompts-file prompts.txt --height 1024 --width 1024 --num-inference-steps 40 \
  --capture-dir captures
python -m sglang.multimodal_gen.tools.dpcache_calibrate plan \
  --capture-dir captures --budgets 12 20 --out-dir schedules
# 2. serve; requests pick a budget with dpcache_budget, or use the default
sglang serve --model-path MODEL --dpcache-schedule-dir schedules --dpcache-default-budget 20
```

## Modifications

- `runtime/cache/dpcache.py`: a BF16 first-order predictor and per-request, per-CFG-branch state. Also PACT calibration costs, an exact DP planner over anchor pairs, and a versioned JSON schedule. The schedule records the checkpoint, scheduler class and config, timesteps and sigmas, resolution, guidance, attention backend and dtype, and a request that doesn't match it is rejected before denoising.
- Schedules belong to the deployment. `--dpcache-schedule-dir` loads the schedules a server serves and checks them against its pipeline, checkpoint and attention backend at startup, so a schedule built for another deployment fails the launch. A request sets `dpcache_budget: K` and the server picks the schedule with that budget calibrated for the request's resolution, step count, scheduler, guidance and dtype. If none fits, the request fails. `--dpcache-default-budget` applies to requests that set no budget and falls back to native where no schedule fits, and `dpcache_budget: 0` opts a request out. `sglang generate --dpcache-budget` and the image/video APIs (extra field) accept the budget.
- `DPCacheMixin` on `CachableDiT`: to opt in, a model sets `_supports_dpcache = True` and routes its block stack through `self.dpcache_blocks(run_blocks)`. The output head stays outside the callable. The model takes no extra arguments; the hook reads the current step and the branch's state from the forward context.
- `DenoisingStage.forward`: checks scope, selects the schedule, attaches fresh state for each CFG branch (`Req.dpcache_states`), and clears it after success or failure. Requests that use no budget take the native path unchanged. A requested budget outside the supported scope fails explicitly; only the server default falls back to native.
- DPCache requests are excluded from dynamic batching: a merged request carries several prompts, and DPCache is calibrated for one. Warmup requests run natively because they use fewer steps than any calibrated schedule.
- Qwen-Image 2.1: `_supports_dpcache = True`, and the block loop moves into `_forward_blocks` without changes.
- Calibration tool (second commit), `python -m sglang.multimodal_gen.tools.dpcache_calibrate`:
  - `record` runs a prompts file natively with the new `dpcache_calibration` request field. The worker scores prediction errors online from each step's final block feature and writes one small capture per prompt; features never leave the worker. It can be sharded across GPUs and resumed.
  - `plan` averages the captures and writes one `K{n}.json` schedule per budget into the directory the server serves.
  - Online and offline scoring share one routine. `dpcache_calibration` writes a file on the worker, so the HTTP APIs do not accept it.
  - Also in this commit: the worker bootstrap's early-import warning no longer reports namespace packages. They run no code, and `python -m sglang.multimodal_gen.tools.<tool>` imports `sglang.multimodal_gen.tools` in every spawned child.
- Docs: `dpcache.mdx` covers scope, the schedule format, the calibration API and how to add a model, and it is listed in the caching overview.

Supported scope for now: BF16, single-image text-to-image, one GPU, eager execution. The following are rejected: CFG, reference images, LoRA, dual-transformer models, torch compile or CUDA graphs, SP/TP/CFG parallelism, and combining DPCache with Cache-DiT, TeaCache, Spectrum, skip-softmax or attention-backend overrides. No calibrated schedule ships with this PR, because a schedule is bound to one checkpoint and request configuration. Operators build one per configuration with the calibration tool.

Review feedback is especially welcome on the serving API (server-owned schedules plus a per-request budget) and on the mixin hook as the integration point for more models.

## Accuracy Tests

- `test_dpcache.py`, `test_dpcache_calibrate.py` and the DPCache cases in `test_qwen_image21_cuda.py`: **158 passed**. The related regression tests (Qwen-Image 2.1, sampling params, SenseNova-U1 scheduler batching, Spectrum, MiniMax-H3 denoise loop, worker bootstrap, layerwise offload, server args), each file run on its own: **559 passed**. All of these ran on the current head, rebased onto `abef3efb6`.
- Requests without DPCache produce output identical to upstream `1d59ce7c9` (checked before the rebase): 8/8 final latents, decoded tensors and PNG bytes match on a real Qwen-Image 2.1 checkpoint.
- End to end on a real Qwen-Image 2.1 checkpoint:
  - The calibration tool, run on the 10 calibration prompts behind the schedules measured below, reproduced them exactly: identical full steps and calibrated costs for every budget from `K=12` to `K=39`. Recording took 2 min 53 s on one RTX 5090 including model load, and the 10 captures total 5 MB.
  - Serving those schedules from `--dpcache-schedule-dir` on the current head reproduced the measured held-out outputs bit for bit on 9 of 9 requests: `K=20` through the server default, `K=12` requested explicitly, and native through `dpcache_budget: 0`.
  - With the default budget, a 768x768 request (no schedule) ran natively. The same request with an explicit `K=20` was rejected with the available schedules listed.
- Quality with a schedule is reported in the table below.

## Speed Tests and Profiling

Setup: Qwen-Image 2.1 BF16 (revision `790c9263`), 1x RTX 5090 32 GB, torch 2.13, 1024x1024, 40 steps, guidance 1.0, `torch_sdpa`, eager, DiT layerwise offload. DPCache schedules were calibrated on 10 prompts, `K` was selected on 8 different prompts, and the Cache-DiT presets were tuned on those same 8. Every choice was frozen before one measurement on 20 fresh held-out prompt/seed pairs. The prompt sets are disjoint.

| Config | Transformer blocks / image | DenoisingStage | E2E | E2E speedup | LPIPS mean / max | PSNR mean / min |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| native | 1280 | 13.26 s | 13.46 s | 1.00x | - | - |
| **DPCache `K=20`** | 640 | 6.63 s | 6.85 s | **1.97x** | **0.0076 / 0.035** | **41.5 / 28.2 dB** |
| Cache-DiT conservative | 710 | 7.47 s | 7.68 s | 1.75x | 0.0159 / 0.042 | 38.1 / 27.8 dB |
| uniform `K=20` (ablation) | 640 | 6.63 s | 6.85 s | 1.97x | 0.070 / 0.208 | 28.3 / 17.2 dB |
| **DPCache `K=12`** | 384 | 3.99 s | 4.20 s | **3.21x** | **0.085** / 0.220 | **27.6** / 17.1 dB |
| Cache-DiT stock | 443 | 4.77 s | 4.98 s | 2.71x | 0.102 / 0.176 | 26.2 / 20.7 dB |
| uniform `K=12` (ablation) | 384 | 3.99 s | 4.20 s | 3.21x | 0.155 / 0.280 | 22.3 / 16.2 dB |

- The two Cache-DiT rows are two settings of the same method. **Stock** is SGLang's Cache-DiT default (`residual_diff_threshold=0.24`, `max_warmup_steps=4`, `max_continuous_cached_steps=3`, `Fn=1`, `Bn=0`). **Conservative** is a stricter preset we picked on the 8 validation prompts to meet a mean/max LPIPS gate of 0.05/0.10 (`residual_diff_threshold=0.12`, `max_warmup_steps=10`, `max_continuous_cached_steps=1`, `Fn=1`, `Bn=1`).
- Each DPCache budget is compared with the Cache-DiT setting of similar quality. `K=20` takes 10.9% less time than conservative Cache-DiT and is closer to native on every quality column. Stock Cache-DiT is faster than `K=20` but much further from native. `K=12` takes 15.6% less time than stock Cache-DiT and has the better mean, but a worse worst case (LPIPS max 0.220 vs 0.176).
- The uniform ablations keep DPCache's budget, first three steps and last full step, and spread the other full steps evenly. They take the same time and are clearly further from native, so the gain comes from the calibrated placement, not only from the budget.
- DenoisingStage is device time averaged over the 20 held-out images. E2E is client wall-clock for a warm generation (encode, denoise, decode, offload transfers), from interleaved paired runs over 4 held-out prompts. Speedup is the paired mean.
- LPIPS (AlexNet) and PSNR compare each image with the native output for the same prompt and seed, after compositing on white.
- With layerwise offload, predicted steps loaded no block weights, and peak memory rose by 154 MB (0.6%). Time scales almost linearly with `K`, because a predicted step costs only the per-step preparation and the output head.
- A low mean LPIPS does not guarantee that every image is preserved. `K=12` rearranged the chairs in a counting prompt and changed the lettering on a sign. `K=20` stayed visually close on every held-out pair.
- One-time cost: about 3 GPU-minutes of calibration per checkpoint and request configuration (10 prompts), plus choosing `K` on a separate validation set.

The benchmark harnesses, frozen corpora, published schedules, the full report and worst-case galleries are in [`fractalyze/sglang@experiment/qwen-image21-dpcache`](https://github.com/fractalyze/sglang/tree/experiment/qwen-image21-dpcache/benchmark/experiments/qwen_image21_dpcache). That branch is not part of this PR. It stacks on an earlier revision of this PR (`2754e6ecf`) that passed the schedule with each request. The inference path is the same, and the served-schedule outputs above are bit-identical to those measurements.

## Checklist

- [x] Format and lint changed code.
- [x] Add unit and CUDA tests for the hook, stage lifecycle, schedule loading and selection, scope checks, batching exclusion, warmup and calibration.
- [x] Update usage and scope documentation.
- [x] Provide accuracy and speed results on the current code.
- [ ] Complete maintainer review and upstream CI before merging.

Development used Claude Code for implementation and Astra for architecture review. Results come from local CPU/CUDA tests and real-model runs as described above.

issues.title: [diffusion] feat: per-layer TP shard planner for DiT linears (--dit-tp-plan)
issues.body:
## Motivation

#29774 shards the Qwen-Image DiT across TP ranks, and the follow-up commits there showed the best per-layer layout is **not** uniform: the text-branch FFN should stay replicated at tp=2 (−8% e2e) but sharded at tp=4 (+1.1% if replicated), the image FFN should be replicated only for small workloads (−18% at 512², regression at ≥1024²), and none of it transfers blindly to other models (the identical change on FLUX's `ff_context` measures +0.8%).

Hardcoding these crossovers per call site does not scale across **TP sizes × machines × models × workloads**. This PR adds a small planner that owns those decisions.

**Why not an analytic cost model?** We tried. Isolated comm/GEMM microbenchmarks mis-rank layouts in both directions: replicating the attention out-projs looks like −8.5% on isolated per-step timings but is e2e-null (+0.8%, mixed-sign ABAB paired diffs — substituting an all-gather for an all-reduce buys nothing); meanwhile the txt_mlp win is far larger than its isolated all-reduce cost (eliminating the collective also removes a sync point and a compile graph break). End-to-end measurement is the only signal that ranked every case correctly, so the design is built around measured rules plus an e2e tuner, not FLOP/bandwidth formulas.

## Design

`--dit-tp-plan {auto | full | aggressive | <plan.json>}` resolves each DiT linear through four levels (first match wins):

1. **Plan-file rules** (`{"rules": {"*.txt_mlp": "replicate"}}`, glob-matched per layer) — exact control; also the output format of the new tuner.
2. **Structural rules** — attention out-projs always shard (their contraction dim is head-sharded; replicate = collective substitution = measured null; ColumnParallel+gather = strictly worse).
3. **`MEASURED_RULES` registry** — per-`(model_family, branch)` defaults that passed e2e ABAB validation, gated on TP degree and (for `aggressive`) the expected workload from `--dit-tp-plan-workload WxH`. Every entry carries its evidence string.
4. **Conservative fallback** — full shard for any un-measured model. The FLUX negative result is the reason this is the default: no blanket architecture rules.

`tools/tune_dit_tp_plan.py` covers machines/models we haven't measured: it boots candidate plans ABAB-interleaved on the actual hardware, compares paired e2e latencies, and emits a plan JSON with provenance (so `--dit-tp-plan tuned.json` is auditable).

`QwenImageTransformerBlock` is the first consumer — its `txt_mlp`/`img_mlp` layouts now come from the planner (replacing the hardcoded `tp<=2` gate, same defaults).

## Measured basis (2×H100, e2e ABAB ×3, single-request)

| setting | full-shard | txt_mlp replicated |
|---|---|---|
| qwen 1024² tp=2 | 5.58 s | **5.12 s (−8%)** |
| qwen 512² tp=2 | ~5.04 s | **4.54 s (−9%)**; +img_mlp → **4.11 s (−18%)** |
| qwen 1536² tp=2 | 10.23 s | 10.28 s (+0.4%) |
| qwen 1024² tp=4 | **6.04 s** | 6.11 s (+1.1%) |
| flux 1024² tp=2 (`ff_context`) | **4.41 s** | 4.44 s (+0.8%) |

## Usage

```bash
# defaults: measured rules for known models, full-shard for unknown
sglang serve --model-path Qwen/Qwen-Image-2512 --tp-size 2 ...

# pinned small-resolution deployment: also replicate the image FFN
sglang serve ... --dit-tp-plan aggressive --dit-tp-plan-workload 512x512

# new machine / new model: tune once, then load the plan
python -m sglang.multimodal_gen.tools.tune_dit_tp_plan \
    --model-path Qwen/Qwen-Image-2512 \
    --serve-args "--num-gpus 2 --tp-size 2 --performance-mode speed --enable-torch-compile" \
    --workload 1024x1024 --candidate full --candidate auto --output tuned.json
sglang serve ... --dit-tp-plan tuned.json
```

## Validation

- `test/unit/test_tp_shard_planner.py`: 14 tests covering the decision chain (registry gates on tp/workload/mode, plan-file override + unsupported-scheme rejection, conservative default, plan loading).
- Smoke on 2×H100: `auto` resolves text-FFN→replicate / image-FFN→shard and serves requests; `full` resolves everything→shard; `aggressive --dit-tp-plan-workload 512x512` adds image-FFN→replicate. Decisions are logged once per layer group with their evidence.
- Perf parity: `auto` at tp=2/tp=4 reproduces exactly the layouts validated in the #29774 measurements above (same module classes, same defaults).

## Notes

Rebased onto `main` now that #29774 has merged — the diff is a clean single commit (planner + `--dit-tp-plan`/`--dit-tp-plan-workload` + qwen wiring + test + offline tuner). Default `auto` reproduces #29774's merged behavior exactly (qwen text-FFN replicate at tp<=2, image-FFN sharded), now expressed as an evidence-carrying measured rule instead of a hardcoded gate.

issues.title: [diffusion] quantization: packed Q/K/V projection for convrot_int8's comfy_kitchen backend
issues.body:
Motivation

Qwen-Image 2.1's QwenImage21Attention projects Q/K/V from one activation with three separate [C, C] linears. convrot_int8 has two kernel backends:

  • the JIT / customkernel backend (CC 9.0 / 10.0 / 12.0 / 12.1), which #38040 already gives a fused single rotation + activation quantisation for q/k/v sharing one input;

  • the comfy_kitchen backend, which serves the GPUs the JIT ops do not build for (CC 8.x Ampere/Ada, CC 10.3) and has no equivalent: every attention block pays two redundant ConvRot activation quantisations and issues three narrow GEMMs.

On a GPU with no FP8/NVFP4 tensor cores -- A100 (CC 8.0), RTX 30/40-series -- the comfy_kitchen backend is not a fallback, it is the only INT8 path, so this gap is real there.

Modifications

  1. layers/quantization/convrot_int8_comfy_kitchen.py: the fused kernel apply ran inline moves to a module-level int8_linear(x, weight, weight_scale, group_size, bias=None, split_out_features=None), and apply becomes a thin adapter. This is a pure refactor: the op, its argument order and its numerics are unchanged, and there is now a single place for the row-split cap. split_out_features lets a packed caller judge the row-split heuristic on the per-projection width instead of the packed width.

  2. models/dits/qwen_image21.py: teach the existing bf16 packing to also cover convrot_int8. The three int8 [C, C] weights and the matching [C, 1] fp32 row scales are re-homed onto one [3C, C] / [3C, 1] storage each, and _project_qkv_packed_convrot_int8 projects all three through a single int8_linear call. A new BitExactFusionGate verifies the first call against the module forwards and falls back on any mismatch, so the packed path can only ever be used when it is bit-exact.

  3. test/unit/test_qwen_image21.py: four new unit tests -- storage sharing keeps values and shares one storage; the packing predicate requires the convrot_int8 method; the consecutive-slice view rejects gaps and separate storages; the packed int8_linear call is bit-exact against the separate per-projection calls at production shapes.

Accuracy Tests

Packed call is bit-exact against the separate calls (max_abs = 0.0); cat(quantize(W_i)) equals quantize(cat(W_i)) exactly. End-to-end on A100 GPU 0 (1024x1024, 40 steps, CFG 1, seed 42), the output PNG md5 is identical to the frozen INT8 baseline: 05288a62012b1353230d53c3297cb67c. The whole flow is inside the existing bit-exact gate, so an unexpected mismatch disables the fusion rather than changing the output.

Speed Tests and Profiling

A100 GPU 0 (CC 8.0, comfy_kitchen backend), Qwen-Image 2.1, 1024x1024 @ 40 steps, CFG 1:

arm | denoise | per step | output md5 -- | -- | -- | -- convrot_int8, unpacked QKV | 9.059 s | -- | 05288a62... convrot_int8, packed QKV (this PR) | 8.796 s | 0.220 s | 05288a62...

Kernel level (M=4114, C=4096, group_size=256): 1.263 ms -> 1.005 ms per attention block (-0.257 ms/block, -8.2 ms/step); the whole saving is the removed ConvRot work.

Scope: on JIT-capable GPUs (H100/H200/Blackwell) the equivalent fusion already exists via the customkernel backend, so this PR is a backend-parity change with no effect there.

issues.title: [Fix] qwen_vl: Neutralize the legacy "<image>" sentinel in chat message text
issues.body:
## Motivation

Fixes #43979.

For models served by `QwenVLImageProcessor` (Qwen2-VL / Qwen2.5-VL / Qwen3-VL / Qwen3.5 / Qwen4-Exp / …), a **literal `<image>` string in ordinary message text** is counted as an image placeholder. `qwen_vl.py` registers the legacy `/generate` sentinel as an alternative inside `image_token_regex`, and the multimodal processor reuses that regex to split and count the rendered prompt. When the same request also carries a real image, the placeholder count exceeds the number of image payloads and the request aborts:

```text
Mismatch: More 'IMAGE' tokens found than corresponding data provided.
Error in request: An exception occurred while loading multimodal data:
...
RuntimeError: An exception occurred while loading multimodal data:
INFO: ... "POST /v1/chat/completions HTTP/1.1" 500 Internal Server Error
```

This is easy to hit in agent workloads: GitHub issue/PR pages render user-uploaded screenshots as the literal text `<image>`, and the fetched page content is replayed as a tool message. Once such a message is in the history, **every** subsequent request to that model fails identically while any image is present — the conversation is permanently wedged (we observed 20+ consecutive 500s from a single agent session, which also tripped the gateway's circuit breaker).

The chat template only ever emits the native `<|vision_start|><|image_pad|><|vision_end|>` placeholder, so in the chat path any bare `<image>` in the rendered prompt is user text.

## Modifications

- `python/sglang/srt/entrypoints/openai/serving_chat.py`
  - Add `neutralize_qwen_vl_image_sentinel*` helpers, mirroring the existing Kimi K3 `neutralize_kimi_k3_image_placeholder*`.
  - Add `self.is_qwen_vl` (model-type gate, same idiom as the existing `is_gpt_oss` / `is_gemma4`).
  - In `_apply_jinja_template()`, neutralize the bare `<image>` sentinel in message text before the chat template is rendered, for the Qwen-VL family only.
  - Only *text* is rewritten: string content, `text` / `input_text` parts, and `reasoning_content` / `reasoning`. Structured `image_url` parts are untouched, so real media still renders as the template's native placeholder and media pairing is unaffected.
  - Raw `/generate` prompts are not touched, so the legacy sentinel keeps working there.
- `test/registered/unit/entrypoints/openai/test_serving_chat.py`
  - `TestNeutralizeQwenVlImageSentinel` covers: text replacement; native placeholder untouched; string content neutralized without mutating the input; text parts neutralized while media parts are preserved; `reasoning_content`; the nested value walker; and gate membership.

Gate list (`QWEN_VL_MODEL_TYPES`) is the set of model types handled by `QwenVLImageProcessor`: `qwen2_vl`, `qwen2_5_vl`, `qwen3_vl`, `qwen3_vl_moe`, `qwen3_5`, `qwen3_5_moe`, `qwen4_exp`, `qwen3_omni_moe`, `intern_s2_preview`, `interns2_mobius`, `cosmos3`.

### Alternatives considered

- **Drop `<image>` from `image_token_regex` / `get_combined_regex()`**: breaks the legacy `/generate` path, where the bare sentinel is the legitimate placeholder written by the caller.
- **Neutralize globally (all models)**: unsafe — LLaVA / DeepSeek-VL2 / InternVL / … legitimately use `<image>` as a *client-written* placeholder in message text, so the gate is required.
- **Degrade the mismatch to a warning in the processor**: masks genuine pairing bugs (e.g. a client that drops image data), so it needs a flag and a separate discussion.

### Related

#37579 reports the same failure mode for the GLM-V (`glm4v`) processor with `<|image|>` / `<|video|>`. This PR only covers the Qwen-VL family; the two share the underlying "prompt split cannot distinguish template placeholders from ordinary text" issue.

## Accuracy Tests

Not applicable — this only rewrites prompt text for the Qwen-VL family; no kernel, model-forward, or sampling change. Covered by a CPU unit test.

## Speed Tests and Profiling

Not applicable — a single `str.replace` pass over message text, gated to the Qwen-VL family.

## Checklist

- [x] Format your code according to the [Format code with pre-commit](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#format-code-with-pre-commit).
- [x] Add unit tests according to the [Run and add unit tests](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#run-and-add-unit-tests).
- [ ] Update documentation according to [Write documentations](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#write-documentations). (No user-facing docs change; behavior matches the chat template's contract.)
- [ ] Provide accuracy and speed benchmark results according to [Test the accuracy](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#test-the-accuracy) and [Benchmark the speed](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#benchmark-the-speed). (N/A, see above.)
- [x] Follow the SGLang code style [guidance](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#code-style-guidance).

## Reproduction (pre-fix)

One real image plus one message whose text contains the literal sentinel:

```python
import requests

PNG = "iVBORw0KGgoAAAANSUhEUgAAAAEAAAABCAYAAAAfFcSJAAAADUlEQVR42mP8z8BQDwAEhQGAhKmMIQAAAABJRU5ErkJggg=="


def call(text):
    return requests.post(
        "http://127.0.0.1:30000/v1/chat/completions",
        json={
            "model": "<any Qwen-VL-family model>",
            "messages": [
                {
                    "role": "user",
                    "content": [
                        {"type": "text", "text": "what is this?"},
                        {"type": "image_url", "image_url": {"url": f"data:image/png;base64,{PNG}"}},
                    ],
                },
                {"role": "tool", "tool_call_id": "c1", "content": text},
                {"role": "user", "content": "go on"},
            ],
            "max_tokens": 8,
        },
    ).status_code


print(call("plain text, no markers"))  # 200
print(call("<image>"))                 # 500 before this change
```

issues.title: [diffusion] feat: overlap declared-parallel pipeline stages
issues.body:
## Motivation

Adjacent conditioning stages such as text encoding, image encoding, and image-VAE encoding can be independent, but pipelines currently execute every stage serially. This PR adds an explicit declaration mechanism and safely overlaps eligible stages.

## Implementation

- `ComposedPipelineBase.add_parallel_stages()` declares one dependency-free execution level.
- `ParallelExecutor` runs eligible replicated stages on the caller stream plus reused side CUDA streams. Every member must opt into `concurrency_safe` and return the same request object.
- `PipelineStage.may_use_collectives` independently declares cross-rank communication. Multiple collective members are placed in declaration-ordered epochs; non-collective siblings can overlap the first epoch without risking rank-dependent NCCL ordering.
- `ImageVAEEncodingStage` reads an explicit VAE capability. Wan VAE reports an encode collective only when spatial-parallel encode is active.
- The residency manager permits a parallel group only when all referenced components are resident. CPU/layerwise offload, non-CUDA execution, unsupported stage paradigms, and `--parallel-stage-execution serial` retain serial execution.
- `serial` is the default. `auto` is explicit because overlap can increase the temporary activation/workspace peak.

## Adoption

Wan I2V and I2V-DMD, Flux2, Qwen Image Edit, Joy Image Edit, MOVA, LongLive2, and the independent LingBot realtime conditioning branches declare applicable parallel groups.

## Validation

- Unit coverage includes execution-level derivation, overlap, ordered collective epochs, payload identity, offload downgrades, grad-mode inheritance, residency contracts, and Wan VAE's SP encode capability.
- Prior H200 E2E measurements: Flux2 Klein Base I2I at 512x512 improved by 6.77% at one step on one GPU, 2.45% at four steps on one GPU, and 6.33% at four steps with TP2; the TP2 output was byte-identical. The same model at 50 steps improved 0.45% while increasing per-rank peak memory by about 1.65 GB. LongLive2 I2V at 832x480x61 and four steps showed no material gain (0.01%).

issues.title: [Fix] [AMD] bugfix: Wan2.2 crash due to Triton kernel compilation
issues.body: ## Summary On gfx1250 with the Triton that ships in the ROCm SDK, `fuse_scale_shift_kernel` silently computed `x * scale + shift` instead of `x * (1 + scale) + shift`, dropping the identity term from adaLN modulation in every DiT block of every diffusion step. Output was wrong but plausible-looking — no crash, no warning. This gates the affected modulation math to fp32 on gfx1250 only. All other targets keep byte-identical codegen. ## Root cause The bug is in Triton's instruction encoding, not in SGLang. gfx1250 is the only target where Triton lowers bf16 elementwise math to packed `v_pk_*_bf16`; every other target promotes to fp32 first. Comparing the two Triton builds for `bf16 + 1.0`: ``` upstream 76940ad3 (fixed): v_pk_add_bf16 v1, v1, 1.0 op_sel:[0,1] ROCm SDK 4cff872c (broken): v_pk_add_bf16 v1, v1, 1.0 op_sel_hi:[1,0] ``` The inline constant `1.0` is the **fp32** pattern `0x3F800000`. Its high half `0x3F80` is bf16 `1.0`; its low half is `0x0000`. The SDK build selects the low half for `src1` in both lanes, so the addend is bf16 zero and the operation becomes a no-op. This affects `+`, `-` and `*` against any AMDGPU hardware inline float constant — `±0.5, ±1.0, ±2.0, ±4.0` — and nothing else. Ordinary literals (`1.5`, `100.0`) are encoded as a packed bf16 pair and are correct; tensor operands are correct. In this kernel `scale_constant` is exactly `1.0`, so it hit the broken case. The bug is fixed in upstream Triton, and `3865efc` (`[AMD] support gfx1250 on ROCM 10`) already moved the gfx1250 image onto a build that carries the fix (`BUILD_TRITON=1`, `TRITON_COMMIT=76940ad3`). This change keeps SGLang correct on the SDK Triton as well, so correctness no longer depends on which Triton the image happens to ship. ## Why fp32 and not `tl.full` `tl.full` looks like it should keep the constant out of the immediate, but it does not — LLVM folds the splat straight back in. Measured on the broken build: | form | result | emitted ISA | |---|---|---| | `scale_constant + scale` | wrong | `v_pk_add_bf16` + inline const | | `tl.full(...) + scale` | wrong | `v_pk_add_bf16` + inline const | | fp32 promote | **correct** | no packed bf16 immediate | fp32 promotion was the only form that produced clean ISA. It also keeps a single rounding on store, matching what the layernorm scale/shift kernels in this same file already do. ## Scope Gated behind `is_gfx1250_supported()` and passed as a `tl.constexpr`, so Triton resolves the branch at compile time — no runtime branch, and the `else` arm is the original code verbatim. NVIDIA, XPU, gfx942 and gfx950 compile to exactly what they did before, including the `tl.full` splat, so their numerics stay bit-identical. `is_gfx1250_supported()` is `lru_cache`d and returns `False` on non-HIP builds without touching CUDA. The kernel is shared by 11 DiT families, so this is not Wan-only: `wanvideo`, `causal_wanvideo`, `hunyuanvideo`, `hunyuan3d`, `qwen_image`, `glm_image`, `joy_image`, `helios`, `lingbot_world`, `longlive2`, `mova_video_dit`. They reach it through `LayerNormScaleShift` / `RMSNormScaleShift` / `ScaleResidualRMSNormScaleShift` with the default `scale_constant=1.0`. The VAE is unaffected — adaLN is a transformer construct, and an ISA scan over a full Wan2.2 run (1307 kernels, 118 using packed bf16) found this kernel as the only affected one. ## Testing After this PR is applied, the video can be played. Extracted pic comparison as below: Tested on rocm/sgl-dev:v0.5.20-rocm10-mi45x-test-triton4cff872c-20260923. Existing unit test `test_scale_shift_4d_matches_torch`, run against both Triton builds: | Configuration | Result | |---|---| | ROCm SDK Triton (broken), with fix | 16 passed | | Upstream Triton (fixed), with fix | 16 passed — no regression | | ROCm SDK Triton, fix reverted | **3 failed** (the bf16 + `scale_constant=1` cases) | | ROCm SDK Triton, gate forced off | **3 failed** — confirms the `else` arm is the original path | End-to-end Wan2.2-T2V-A14B on the broken SDK Triton (720×1280, 193 frames, 8 steps, seed 42) completed cleanly and matches a known-good baseline generated on the fixed Triton: correlation **0.991**, PSNR **29.3 dB**, mean abs diff 4.3/255. A dropped identity term collapses structure, so this margin is rounding and sampling non-determinism, not lost conditioning. Performance is unchanged. `bench_scale_shift_4d.py`, 3 runs each way, medians: 117.7 vs 119.9 µs (wan), 16.23 vs 16.24 µs (longlive). Within-group spread was ±20% on the larger workloads, so those deltas are noise — the kernel reads three tensors and writes one with no reuse, so it is bandwidth-bound and the extra `v_cvt` ops hide behind memory latency. ## Checklist - [ ] Format your code according to the [Format code with pre-commit](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#format-code-with-pre-commit). - [ ] Add unit tests according to the [Run and add unit tests](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#run-and-add-unit-tests). - [ ] Update documentation according to [Write documentations](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#write-documentations). - [ ] Provide accuracy and speed benchmark results according to [Test the accuracy](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#test-the-accuracy) and [Benchmark the speed](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#benchmark-the-speed). - [ ] Follow the SGLang code style [guidance](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#code-style-guidance). ## Review and Merge Process 1. issues.title: [Perf] [AMD] diffusion: add a Triton dense attention prefill path for gfx1151
issues.body:
## Motivation

`SDPAImpl.forward` transposes the token-major q/k/v to head-major and hands SDPA a
**non-contiguous** view. On gfx1151 that view costs AOTriton a lot: the same
`attn_fwd` kernel runs at 12.4 / 6.7 / 2.06 TF for 4096 / 8192 / 16384 tokens,
versus 12.4 → 18 TF when the operands are dense. Even the dense number leaves
throughput on the table: a plain Triton prefill kernel reaches 31.8 TF at the
same shape, which is the bulk of diffusion prefill cost.

## What this adds

* `python/sglang/kernels/ops/diffusion/attention/flash_attn_dense_triton.py` — a
  non-causal MHA prefill kernel for dense `[B, H, S, D]` operands. It needs no
  masks in the main loop (query length is a multiple of the tile, padding rows of
  K/V are zeroed and their mass is subtracted from the denominator), loads K
  pre-transposed through its strides, and runs `BLOCK_M = BLOCK_N = 64` with 4
  warps and a single pipeline stage. bf16 in, fp32 accumulate, bf16 out; softmax
  keeps the reference's rounding (unscaled q into the WMMA,
  `1/sqrt(D) * log2(e)` on the fp32 scores).
* A gated fast path in `SDPAImpl.forward`: HIP only, `SGLANG_USE_ROCM_TRITON_DENSE_ATTN`
  (default off), bf16, batch 1, equal q/k/v lengths, `head_dim == 128`,
  `seq_len % 64 == 0`, `seq_len >= 4096`, non-causal, no dropout. Everything
  else falls through to the existing SDPA call untouched. Operands are
  materialised head-major once before the kernel sees them; below 4096 tokens
  those copies cost more than the kernel saves, so shorter sequences stay on
  SDPA.

## Numbers (Ryzen AI MAX 395, gfx1151, torch 2.9.1+rocm7.2.4, B=1 H=32 D=128 bf16)

Same dense head-major operands for both, kernel-only (median of 10, 3 warmups):

| seq | AOTriton SDPA | Triton | speedup | Triton TF |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 4096 | 16.4 ms | 9.7 ms | 1.70x | 28.5 |
| 16384 | 239.3 ms | 138.5 ms | 1.73x | 31.8 |

The 16384 row uses the shipped one-stage pipeline; the 4096 row predates the
stage sweep and is unaffected by it.

What the flag actually changes end to end, i.e. including the layout
materialisation the kernel needs versus the strided call the backend makes today:

| seq | today (SDPA on the view) | with this PR | speedup |
|---|---|---|---|
| 4096 | 22.2 ms | 16.6 ms | 1.34x |
| 8192 | 163.6 ms | 54.3 ms | 3.01x |
| 16384 | 2131 ms | 183.3 ms | 11.6x |

The 16K row is the interesting one: AOTriton's strided-operand regression grows
faster than the work does, so at 128 head dim the gap widens with sequence
length. Diffusion DiT self-attention at 2048x2048 sits exactly there.

## Kernel resources and scaling

Compiled at S=16384 the kernel uses 256 VGPR per lane (the RDNA3 limit) with
**zero spills** and 16 KiB of LDS, which keeps four CTAs resident per CU. A
second pipeline stage doubles LDS to 32 KiB, halves residency, and measured
146.3 ms instead of 138.5 ms — that is why the shipped configuration uses one
stage. Of 81 swept `BLOCK_M x BLOCK_N x warps x stages` points, 66 compiled and
this one ranked first; `BLOCK_M = 128` with 2-4 warps spills 350-1149 registers
and drops to 3.8-6.7 TF.

Sweeping the sequence length shows where the materialisation stops paying:

| seq | SDPA on the view | this PR | speedup | kernel vs dense AOTriton |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 1024 | 1.37 ms | 2.10 ms | 0.65x | 1.81x |
| 2048 | 5.39 ms | 5.58 ms | 0.97x | 1.78x |
| 4096 | 21.7 ms | 16.9 ms | 1.29x | 1.70x |
| 8192 | 150.2 ms | 54.2 ms | 2.77x | 1.62x |
| 16384 | 2180.5 ms | 182.4 ms | 11.95x | 1.64x |
| 32768 | 12932.8 ms | 658.6 ms | 19.64x | 1.65x |

The kernel alone wins at every length (1.62-1.81x against dense AOTriton, and
2.1x to 22x against the strided view); what crosses over is the three
materialisations, which are 69% of the call at 1024 tokens and 20% at 16384.
Hence the 4096-token floor.

Numerics against an fp32 reference: max abs diff 1.1e-3, mean 1.9e-5, no element
above 0.05 (bf16 rounding on both sides).

## Tests

* `test/registered/unit/attention/test_sdpa_triton_dense_attention.py` (CPU, no GPU
  needed; the kernel is mocked): env gate, non-ROCm, torch.compile, causal,
  dropout, fp32, `head_dim != 128`, `seq % 64`, short sequences (`seq < 4096`),
  mismatched lengths, kernel refusal → SDPA fallback; operand strides and `scale`
  forwarded to the kernel. `10 passed`.
* `test/registered/kernels/ops/attention/test_flash_attn_dense_triton.py` (AMD CI):
  fp32-reference numerics at 128/256/512 tokens, zero-padded K/V with `kv_pad`,
  predicate rejections. `4 passed` on gfx1151.

Both were run on gfx1151 with `PYTHONPATH` pointed at a patched copy of the
installed package, so they are not compile-only checks.

## Relation to other work

* #46065 materialises dense SDPA operands; that closes the "strided view" half of
  the gap (AOTriton back to 240 ms at 16K) but not the remaining 1.63x.
* Model-side qkv changes and sparse-attention kernels are out of scope here.

## Caveats

- The default is off: only gfx1151 has been measured. gfx11 should behave the
  same, gfx9x untested — flip the default once there are numbers.
- Sequences below 4096 tokens deliberately stay on SDPA. The floor is the
  measured crossover from the table above, not a derived bound: the kernel alone
  is faster at every length, but the three head-major materialisations dominate
  short calls and make the full path a net loss there.
- End-to-end diffusion (Qwen-Image 2.1 at 2048x2048) throughput is not measured
  in this PR; the benchmark above is operator-level.

issues.body:
## Motivation

Add native text-to-image inference for [Ovis-Image 7B](https://huggingface.co/ATH-MaaS/Ovis-Image-7B) (Diffusers format). It is available through `sglang generate` and the OpenAI-compatible image API. `ATH-MaaS/Ovis-Image-7B`, the legacy `AIDC-AI/Ovis-Image-7B`, and local Diffusers component directories all resolve to the native pipeline. Defaults follow the official recipe: 1024 × 1024, 50 steps, CFG 5, 256 text tokens, BF16.

## Modifications

**Model and pipeline**
- Native Ovis DiT: 6 dual-stream and 27 single-stream blocks, context RMSNorm, SwiGLU, and the official weight mapping. Value/gate and attention/MLP output weights keep their own TP partitions.
- Reuses native Qwen3, AutoencoderKL, the shared denoising and residency stages, packed FLUX latents, and the conditioning cache.
- Follows the official prompt template, prefix masking, fixed-length text attention, dynamic scheduler shift, and `[A,A,B,B]` multi-output ordering.
- Supports serial and parallel CFG, DiT TP, Ulysses and Ring SP, and component/layerwise offload, with no new production CLI flags.
- Image editing, single-file weights, quantization, LoRA, caching accelerators, `torch.compile`, and breakable CUDA graphs are rejected with explicit errors.

**Numerics.** The goal is that single-GPU runs match pinned Diffusers bit for bit, and parallel runs stay within the reference's own noise.
- The QK RMSNorm rounds to BF16 before the FP32 RoPE, as the official `nn.RMSNorm` does. This is Ovis opt-in; FLUX defaults are unchanged.
- **Row-parallel projections**: TP row projections in the Ovis DiT (`OvisImageRowParallelLinear`) all-reduce FP32 partial products and round once with the bias, which is what the dense GEMM does. Reducing BF16 partials alone already puts short-text first predictions outside the BF16 tolerance; that was measured on one GPU with a K-split emulation.
- **Flash split-KV**: PyTorch flash attention switches to split-KV once `B·H·⌈Sq/128⌉ < 0.8·SMs`. TP and Ulysses shrink the local head count, so at short sequence lengths the shards take a different summation order than the full-head reference. On B200, at seq 1025, 24 heads and 12/6-head shards differ in 1.29M elements; at seq 4224 they match exactly. `OvisImageSDPAImpl` pads query rows past the threshold, but only when the full-head model would not split. This restores bitwise per-head equality, which a unit test checks.
- **Tail padding**: Ulysses tail-padded attention trims the padding after the all-to-all instead of masking it.
- Ovis-only, opt-in HF-compatible Qwen TP numerics. Text-encoder row projections gather the input and weight and run the full-K GEMM.

**Shared code**
- **VAE**: `AutoencoderKLMixin` now runs each tile of a tiled decode through spatial-parallel decode. Inputs shorter than the decode world size fall back to local decode. Before this, tiled + spatial decode called the sharded decoder on whole tiles. The Flux2 KL VAE shares this mixin and gets the same fix.
- **USP**: fixes receive-buffer ownership for sequential unpacked FP32 Q/K/V collectives.

**Tests and docs**
- Unit tests in `python/sglang/multimodal_gen/test/unit/` cover component numerics against the official small models, the TP and attention numerics above, config, the validator, USP buffers, and tiled spatial VAE on real Gloo groups.
- A B200 HTTP e2e test.
- A manual oracle and multi-GPU runner in `test/manual/diffusion/`. It requests `quality="exact"` by default, because the serving default `lossless` mounts VAE fast paths that only move rounding.
- Cookbook page, catalog entry.

Attribution and sources: [official transformer](https://github.com/huggingface/diffusers/blob/c6df88a511a98740646ee55577b590c9852650ce/src/diffusers/models/transformers/transformer_ovis_image.py), [official pipeline](https://github.com/huggingface/diffusers/blob/c6df88a511a98740646ee55577b590c9852650ce/src/diffusers/pipelines/ovis_image/pipeline_ovis_image.py), [checkpoint](https://huggingface.co/ATH-MaaS/Ovis-Image-7B/tree/41be1c5821a92c970d63d7eb595a2fd3fe32b22e).

## Accuracy Tests

**Setup**
- Pins: checkpoint `41be1c58`, independent official Diffusers `c6df88a5`.
- Inputs: identical CPU initial latents. Reference SDPA excludes cuDNN, matching the native platform policy.
- Tolerances are unchanged: BF16 `atol=0.05, rtol=0.02`; FP32 `1e-4`.
- Commit: every result below is from this branch's HEAD, on B200, with a clean tree.

**Single GPU (exact tier)**
| Check | Result |
|---|---|
| 512² L1/L64 and 1024²/50 quality scenes | Conditioning, every prediction, the full trajectory, and the decoded images are bit-exact vs official (PSNR ∞) |
| CFG2 L64 | Bit-exact |
| Same-latent dense VAE decode | Bit-exact vs official |

**Parallel, first predictions at the original tolerance**
| Topology | max abs / out-of-tolerance |
|---|---|
| L1 512² TP2 | 0.049 / 0 |
| L1 512² Ulysses2 | 0.016 / 0 |
| L1 512² TP2 × Ulysses2 | 0.049 / 0 |
| 1024² TP2 × Ulysses2 | 0.031 / 0 |

**Later steps against the noise baseline.** A late-step same-input check at the original tolerance cannot tell a parallel bug from evaluation-order noise. On a single GPU, changing only the FP32 summation order already puts step 49 at 496 out-of-tolerance elements.

We therefore gate the same-input four-GPU TP2 × Ulysses2 replay (1024², steps 0/11/12/49) against single-GPU controls:
- The controls are efficient-kernel SDPA, split-K with FP32 reduction, and split-K with BF16 reduction.
- Rule: per step, take the worse CFG branch. Max abs and the out-of-tolerance count must not exceed the worst control; RMSE must stay within 1.05× of it, because RMSE saturates at the BF16 floor.

| Step | TP2 × SP2 (max / count / rmse) | Worst control |
|---|---|---|
| 0 | 0.031 / 0 / 0.0044 | 0.031 / 0 / 0.0051 |
| 11 | 0.039 / 0 / 0.0057 | 0.148 / 23 / 0.0071 |
| 12 | 0.137 / 2 / 0.0065 | 0.270 / 93 / 0.0079 |
| 49 | 0.219 / 1693 / 0.0200 | 0.375 / 2242 / 0.0223 |

**Spatial VAE (same latent).** Raw decoder output has 17 out-of-tolerance values at max 0.090. The worst control (cuDNN autotune) is at 45 / 0.098, so this is within noise. Decoded images pass at the original tolerance.

**Runtime matrix.** All cases pass:
- single GPU, no-CFG, batch 2, prompt batch;
- component and layerwise offload;
- tiny TP2, tiny Ulysses2, tiny TP2 × SP2;
- TP2, Ulysses2, Ring2, CFG2, TP2 × SP2;
- tiled and spatial VAE;
- the HTTP lifecycle.

The cookbook HTTP recipe (1024²/50, one GPU) passes in 7.9 s including HTTP. Unit tests: 64 passed, 2 skipped.

## Visual comparison

1024 × 1024, 50 steps, CFG 5, seed 42, CPU generator, exact quality tier. All runs use the same initial latents. Reference is official Diffusers `c6df88a5`; columns are SGLang on 1 GPU, TP2 and Ulysses2 (2 × B200). The bottom row shows the mean absolute RGB error against the official image, amplified 8×.

- **1 GPU**: bit-exact, so the diff map is black.
- **TP2 and Ulysses2**: both pass the first-prediction gate at the original tolerance. Their later steps drift within the BF16 noise floor, which shows up as small content shifts rather than artifacts.

Prompt: 一个温暖的咖啡馆门口，木制招牌写着“欢迎光临”，电影写实摄影。

![Ovis-Image scene 0](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/fusheng-ji/sglang/61769368c593c22a26a108cc14326b9220a13b2c/ovis-image-scene-0.jpg)

Prompt: A red bicycle leaning against a stone wall beside a quiet lake at sunset, realistic photography.

![Ovis-Image scene 1](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/fusheng-ji/sglang/61769368c593c22a26a108cc14326b9220a13b2c/ovis-image-scene-1.jpg)

| Topology | Scene 0 PSNR / SSIM | Scene 1 PSNR / SSIM |
|---|---|---|
| 1 GPU | ∞ / 1.0000 | ∞ / 1.0000 |
| TP2 | 28.05 / 0.9408 | 37.72 / 0.9731 |
| Ulysses2 | 27.02 / 0.9232 | 36.95 / 0.9685 |

## Speed Tests and Profiling

The FP32 TP reduction doubles row-projection all-reduce traffic.

| Configuration | BF16 reduction | FP32 reduction (this PR) |
|---|---|---|
| TP2, 1024², 50 steps, 2 × B200 (s/step, median of 4) | 0.083 | 0.099 |

Query padding only triggers at short sequences and does not run at 1024². These are DiT-step timings, not a serving benchmark.

## Follow-ups (not in this PR)

- The flash split-KV head-count dependence affects any DiT that shards heads at short sequence lengths, for example FLUX, Qwen-Image, and Anima. The shared fix is in #43242 (`SDPAImpl` / `USPAttention`, exact tier). Whichever PR lands second will switch `OvisImageSDPAImpl` to the shared implementation.
- `.github/workflows/_pr-test-check-changes.yml` still references the old `test/registered/unit/diffusion` path. This predates this branch.

## Checklist

- [x] Format code with pre-commit.
- [x] Add unit tests.
- [x] Update documentation (cookbook page, catalog).
- [x] Provide accuracy and speed results.
- [x] Follow the SGLang code style guidance.

### Update (2026-10-14)

- **Fixed an import broken by the previous `main` merge.** `ovis_image.py` still imported `qwen_image._pack_latents`, which #43064 removed, so the Ovis-Image config failed to import. It now uses `base.pack_latents_2x2`, which computes the same packing.
- **Merged current `main`.** Breakable CUDA graph conflict: `main` now keeps an explicit graph request on unvalidated models with a warning. Ovis-Image still rejects it through `validate_breakable_cuda_graph`, which now runs before that warning, and the config test follows `main`'s policy for other models.
- **Strict FP32 VAE oracles.** The FLUX.2 VAE parallel check now turns TF32 off in a scope on each rank for the strict FP32 oracle (restored on exit, nesting and exceptions) and keeps the 1e-4 tolerance; BF16 is checked separately under the production policy.

Validation on the merged head: Ovis-Image unit tests 37 passed, 2 skipped, 153 subtests passed. FLUX.2 VAE two-GPU check with full weights (tiled, tail tiles, tiny fallback, recovery): 8 cases per rank, all within tolerance, weights loaded strictly. `test_server_args.py` has the same 3 failures on this branch and on a clean `main` checkout (`c82e8bd5fe`), both 3 failed / 232 passed: two cold-import subprocess timeouts on our loaded host and an HF cache permission error. The two tokenizer-oracle tests that skip without a checkpoint were also run, with the local Ovis-Image-7B checkpoint: `test_ovis_image_config.py` 15 passed, none skipped.

The VAE check prints 60 `CUDACachingAllocator ... failed with OOM` warnings under the default allocator: each is one 138.8 GB request failing while the process already caches about 143 GB (most likely a cuDNN workspace probe; the call site was not captured). With `PYTORCH_NO_CUDA_MEMORY_CACHING=1` there are no warnings and the same 8 cases per rank pass, so the warnings do not hide a failure. fp32 results differ slightly between the two runs (up to 1.3e-5 against the 1e-4 tolerance), so they are not bit-identical.

close Issue #34211 

## Motivation

Fixes startup failure when serving ModelSlim-quantized Qwen3.5 NEXTN checkpoints on NPU, where the MTP (draft) module is stored unquantized (all `mtp.*` entries in `quant_model_description.json` are `FLOAT`) while the main model is `W8A8_DYNAMIC`.

Additionally fixes a runtime crash on the first inference request due to Ascend UB overflow in the mamba state scatter kernel.

## Modifications

**1. ModelSlim MoE unquantized fallback (`modelslim.py`)**
- `get_quant_method`: Use `is_layer_skipped` before `get_moe_scheme` and return `None` only when every expert projection is explicitly marked `FLOAT`
- Preserve `get_moe_scheme` validation and `ValueError` handling for missing, mixed, or unsupported schemes

**2. MTP whole-model unquant detection (`qwen3_5_mtp.py`)**  
- Add ModelSlim branch to `_mtp_quant_config` helper that detects when all `mtp.*` entries are `FLOAT` and drops `quant_config` entirely
- This ensures the bf16 MoE dispatch overrides in `forward()` (`SGLANG_DEEPEP_BF16_DISPATCH`, `DEEP_NORMAL_MODE_USE_INT8_QUANT`) are triggered

**3. UB-aware mamba scatter (`ascend_hybrid_linear_attn_backend.py`)**
- Compute `h_block_size` dynamically from Ascend UB budget (192KB) instead of hardcoding `h_block_size=2`
- For this model (V=128, K=128, fp32), the tile is 128KB single-buffered but Bisheng multi-buffer pass doubles it to 256KB, exceeding 192KB UB
- The computed `h_block_size=1` brings the tile to 64KB single / 128KB double, fitting within budget
- Add warning when a single (V,K) plane already overflows UB

## Accuracy Tests

**Before:** 
- Startup fails with `ValueError: Unsupported ModelSlim MoE schemes for layer mtp.layers.0.mlp.experts: W13='FLOAT', W2='FLOAT'`
- After workaround with `--speculative-draft-model-quantization unquant`, first request crashes with `error: ub overflow, requires 2097152 bits while 1572864 bits available!`
